property_summary: Only calls from DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT can successfully set number via setL1BlockValues, so for any caller other than the depositor the call reverts.
Only the depositor address can successfully call setL1BlockValues (calls from non-depositor revert).

For any call to setL1BlockValues by the depositor, the reference contract sets the hash state variable to the provided _hash value before (i.e. at or no later than) all other state updates complete during the call; the mutant delays assigning hash until after other fields, allowing intermediate observers to see a different ordering and causing hash() to differ for some interleavings (e.g., a reentrant observer that reads hash mid-call).

For any inputs and any depositor caller, C always ensures that the public getter `hash()` returns the value supplied as `_hash` to setL1BlockValues immediately (i.e. after the external call completes `c.hash()` == `_hash` for all inputs); the mutant that assigns `hash` last can be observed (via a reentrant helper that reads `hash` during the call) to produce a differing final stored value for some fuzzed inputs, breaking this rule.

For every admissible input and depositor caller, after setL1BlockValues returns the contract's public getter hash() equals the _hash argument passed; the mutant that assigns hash last can be observed (via a reentrant depositor helper that calls back into c during setL1BlockValues) to make the final stored hash differ for some fuzzed inputs.

For any inputs and when called by the depositor, setL1BlockValues always results in c.hash() equaling the _hash argument after the call returns; the mutant that moves the assignment to hash to the end can be observed (via a reentrant depositor helper that calls back while setL1BlockValues is executing) to produce a different final hash for some fuzzed inputs.

For any calldata inputs and when setL1BlockValues is invoked by the designated DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT, the reference C ensures that the public getter `hash()` equals the `_hash` argument immediately after the call returns; the mutant that moves the assignment to `hash` to the end can be distinguished by a reentrant depositor helper that during execution changes some other field and then on return causes the final stored `hash` to differ, so the property is violated for some fuzzed inputs.

Only the designated DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT can change sequenceNumber (i.e., after a call to setL1BlockValues by msg.sender, c.sequenceNumber() equals the provided _sequenceNumber only if msg.sender == c.DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT()).
